samples.summary: `imageKeyHandler` runs ahead of the view-only gate and never checks `readOnly`, so its document-mutating branches sit outside the only client-side write gate
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.handleKeyDown` dispatches to `this.imageKeyHandler(e)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:838, which is *before* the `if (this.readOnly)` block at text-editor.ts:867 documented as the thing that keeps the document unmutatable for viewers. The handler this change rewrites (editor.ts:2249-2367) contains no `readOnly` check at all, while its Delete/Backspace branch calls `docStore.snapshot(); doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1)` (editor.ts:2282-2283) and the new cut branch installs a text selection over the image (editor.ts:2348) whose deletion is prevented only by the separate guard inside `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1195). `YorkieDocStore` performs no role check of its own (no `readOnly`/`role` match in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts), and the server-side Yorkie auth webhook that would deny the `rw` verb for a `viewer` share link only enforces when `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, shadow-allow at :97-105). So for a share-link viewer (`readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:278) on a default deployment the client flag *is* the enforcement, and anything that populates `selectedImage` while read-only turns one Delete/Backspace keystroke into an unauthorized edit that CRDT-replicates to editors. The change adds four new early-return branches to this handler and adds no `readOnly` guard, and none of the new tests in packages/docs/test/view/image-copy.test.ts construct a read-only editor.

samples.summary: `EditorAPI.selectImageAt` has no `readOnly` guard, unlike `updateSelectedImage`, and is the only remaining way to reach the ungated image-key mutation path in a view-only document
samples.evidence: `selectImageAt` (editor.ts:3662-3669) sets `selectedImage` with no `readOnly` check, while the neighbouring `updateSelectedImage` opens with `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:3688) and the pointer path `handleImageMouseDown` opens with `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2477). That asymmetry leaves one unguarded entry point into image-selection state: any embedder (or future toolbar / context-menu / comment-jump wiring) that calls `editor.selectImageAt(...)` in a view-only doc arms the `imageKeyHandler` path, whose Delete/Backspace branch writes to the document (editor.ts:2283) before `TextEditor`'s read-only gate is consulted (text-editor.ts:838 vs :867). I could not complete the chain against shipped UI code — grepping the repo for `selectImageAt` finds only the interface declaration, the implementation, the new tests and design docs, no frontend call site — so this is a latent gate hole rather than a live bypass today; the new tests drive `selectImageAt` directly, which is exactly the shape a future caller would take.

samples.summary: The new cut promotion installs a deletable text selection before any permission check, leaning entirely on a single downstream guard
samples.evidence: On Cmd/Ctrl+X the new branch calls `selection.setRange({ anchor: { blockId, offset }, focus })` (editor.ts:2348) and returns `false` so the browser's `cut` event fires. In a view-only session the only thing stopping the resulting `cut` from calling `deleteSelection()` is `if (this.readOnly)` at the top of `handleCut` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1195). Establishing destructive state first and relying on one downstream check is fragile ordering: any future path that consumes a live selection (a context-menu 'Cut', a programmatic `deleteSelection`, a paste handler) would act on a selection the read-only user was never allowed to create. A `readOnly` short-circuit at the top of `imageKeyHandler` would make the promotion unreachable rather than merely harmless.

verdict.reason: The finding's exploit chain is broken at its first link. `imageKeyHandler` starts with `if (!selectedImage) return false;` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2250), so every mutating branch is gated on `selectedImage` being populated. I enumerated all writes to `selectedImage` repo-wide: the only production path that sets it non-null is `handleImageMouseDown` at editor.ts:2531, whose first statement is `if (readOnly) return;` at editor.ts:2477 — and `findImageAtPoint` is called exactly once in the whole package (editor.ts:2524), inside that guarded function. The only other non-null assignment is the `selectImageAt` API at editor.ts:3667, which a repo-wide grep shows is called nowhere outside packages/docs/test/view/image-copy.test.ts. `readOnly` is a fixed initialize-time parameter (editor.ts:919, supplied at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:327) with no setter, so it cannot flip mid-session. Therefore a share-link viewer can never have a selected image, `imageKeyHandler` returns false immediately, and the key falls through to the `if (this.readOnly)` gate at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:867. The Delete/Backspace `doc.deleteText` (editor.ts:2283) and the new cut-branch `selection.setRange` (editor.ts:2348) are unreachable in read-only mode. Sibling image mutation surfaces are independently gated (dragover 2581, drop 2589, insertImage 3614, updateSelectedImage 3688, API-boundary no-op list 3833-3851). The absent in-handler check is defense-in-depth, not a reachable authorization bypass.

verdict.reason: No readOnly guard exists for `selectImageAt` anywhere on its path. editor.ts:3662-3669 sets `selectedImage` with no check, while `updateSelectedImage` (3688) and `handleImageMouseDown` (2477) both gate on `readOnly`. The view-only API neutralization block (editor.ts:3833-3851), which exists precisely because "the programmatic EditorAPI ... is reachable by any holder of `api`", lists insertImage/updateSelectedImage/cut/paste/etc. but omits `selectImageAt`. The state it arms is ungated end-to-end: `imageKeyHandler` is installed under a bare `if (textEditor)` (2210), its Delete/Backspace branch writes via `docStore.snapshot(); doc.deleteText(...)` (2279-2290) with no readOnly check, and TextEditor dispatches it at text-editor.ts:838 before its readOnly gate at :867, with the keydown listener registered unconditionally at :544. The server-side viewer write denial (backend yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200) cannot be cited as an existing guard because it is bypassed in shadow mode unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE==='true' (:86-105). `initialize` (editor.ts:915) returns `api` with no further wrapper. Latent (no shipped caller), but the gate hole is real and in-lane.
